name: Daemon, Chenoodaemon
body:
Chenoodaemon CR 3

Each time this terrifying creature exhales, the air radiates an unearthly chill.

XP 800
NE Large outsider (daemon, cold, evil, native)
Init +5; Senses darkvision 60 ft., lifesense 60 ft., snow vision; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 10, flat-footed 14 (+1 Dex, +5 natural, -1 size)
hp 30 (4d10+8); fast healing 1 (fire, see frostbound)
Fort +5, Ref +2, Will +6
DR 5/good; Immune acid, cold, death effects, disease, poison; Resist electricity 10; Weaknesses vulnerability to fire

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee bite +6 (1d8+6 plus 1d6 cold)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Spell-Like Abilities (Cl 6th; concentration +8)

3/day—winter grasp
1/day—frigid touch

STATISTICS

Str 18, Dex 12, Con 14, Int 10, Wis 16, Cha 18
Base Atk +3; CMB +8 (includes +1 size bonus); CMD 19 (includes +1 size bonus)
Feats Blood Feastha, Improved Initiative
Skills Climb +11, Intimidate +11, Knowledge (planes) +4, Perception +10, Stealth +4 (includes -4 size penalty), Survival +10, Swim +10
Languages Common, those known in life, telepathy 100 ft.

Sq icy bite, tundra stride

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Cold Hearted (Su)

When a chenoodaemon dies, it expels a heart made of ice from its mouth which bursts into millions of tiny ice shards. The ice shards deal 4d6 cold damage to all creatures within a 10-foot radius of the chenoodaemon. A successful DC 14 Reflex saving throw halves the damage. The shards immediately melt 1 round later.

Frostbound (Ex)

A chenoodaemon’s fast healing only works in temperatures of 40 degrees Fahrenheit or less.

Chenoodaemons can’t regain hit points lost from fire damage and they are considered to always be under the effects of endure elements with regard to cold climates.

Hunger Pangs (Su)

3/d A chenoodaemon can give voice to its hunger by issuing a terrifying bellow from its mouth as a swift action. All creatures within a 60- foot radius must make a successful DC 14 Will saving throw or gain the shaken condition for 1 minute. A creature that makes its save is immune to this ability for 24 hours. The save DC for this fear effect is Charisma-based. Creatures immune to fear are immune to this ability.

Icy Bite (Su)

A chenoodaemon’s bite is supernaturally cold. It deals an extra 1d6 cold damage with each successful bite.

Snow Vision (Ex)

A chenoodaemon’s vision is not hindered in snowy conditions; it does not take any penalties on Perception checks due to snow, sleet, or hail.

Tundra Stride (Ex)

A chenoodaemon can move across snow and ice without penalty and does not need to make Acrobatics checks to run or charge on ice.

ECOLOGY

Environment tundra
Organization solitary
Treasure none

Anger-filled, glowing red eyes provide a sharp contrast to this unclothed creature’s pale, blue-tinged skin. Its face is a grotesque sight with chewed off lips and an enormous fanged maw. Though a chenoodaemon’s stooped posture might cause its prey to think it frail or slow, it is actually quite powerful with legs and arms as thick as tree stumps. Chenoodaemons stand 8-9 feet tall and weigh 500-600 pounds.

When a humanoid that is dying of starvation in the tundra makes a pact with a harbinger of the horseman of famine, it becomes a chenoodaemon upon its mortal death. The harbinger promises the creature to be forever free from the ravages of cold and to feast to its heart’s desire. Individuals that accept this bargain are destined to roam the tundra forever as flesh-eating cannibals with no mercy for the pain they inflict. Ironically, though the cold has no power to harm a chenoodaemon as promised, heat causes it extreme distress— so much so that the chenoodaemon prowls the tundra naked and sleeps below a blanket of snow each night.

Though a chenoodaemon is gifted with a powerful and deadly physique, making it an apex predator of the tundra and able to feast upon all of the native fauna, its hunger is never satiated. Always angry and always hungry, a chenoodaemon is constantly on the prowl looking for its next meal.

Lost Atlanteans, Copyright 2024, Bloodstone Press; author Beth Jones
